rp and strength.question: Should I use the [$t(rp)] tab or the [$t(strength2)] tab?
rp and strength.answer:
If you are new, the [$t(rp)] tab shows less information and lets you compare Pokémon more simply.

The [$t(strength2)] tab, on the other hand, lets you check strength, ingredient count, and skill count in detail while changing the conditions.

Once you get used to the tool, we recommend comparing Pokémon on the [$t(strength2)] tab with parameter values set to match your own play style.

rp and strength difference.question: What is the difference between the [$t(rp)] tab and the [$t(strength2)] tab?

daytime performance.question: How can I check performance for daytime play?
daytime performance.answer:
On the [$t(strength2)] tab, change the [$t(1day)] setting to [$t(8hours)] or similar.

This lets you compare performance when you can tap frequently during the day.

compare new pokemon.question: How should I compare a Pokémon I have just caught?
compare new pokemon.answer:
First, add the Pokémon you have already raised or plan to raise to your box.
1. Select [$t(strength2)] for the top tab and [$t(box)] for the bottom tab.
1. Add the Pokémon you caught to the box.
1. Change the box sort order to the metric you want to compare (such as [$t(total strength)], [$t(ingredient)], or [$t(skill)]).
1. Use the box order to see which Pokémon is stronger.

Tips
* Changing [$t(current level)] at the bottom-left of the box lets you compare strength at a specific level.
* Changing the tap frequency can sometimes reverse the results, so compare carefully.
* Results can also flip depending on the expert mode or event bonus, so consider carefully.
* For berry Pokémon, setting the tap frequency to [$t(none)] lets you compare strength while sneaky snacking.

compare expert mode.question: This week I moved to an Expert-mode research area, and I want to know which Pokémon can perform well.
compare expert mode.answer:
First, register your Pokémon in the box at their current level.
1. Select [$t(strength2)] for the top tab and [$t(box)] for the bottom tab.
1. Set the research area and favorite berry.
1. Change the box sort order to the metric you want to compare (such as [$t(total strength)], [$t(ingredient)], or [$t(skill)]).
1. Use the box order to see which Pokémon will perform well.

box edit.question: How do I edit a Pokémon in the box?
box edit.answer:
Press and hold the icon of the Pokémon you want to edit.

If you only want to change the level, it is easier to change [$t(level)] in the [$t(parameter)] section.

box delete.question: How do I delete a Pokémon from the box?
box delete.answer:
1. Select the Pokémon you want to delete.
1. Press the [︙] icon that appears at the top-right of the Pokémon.
1. Choose [$t(delete)] from the menu.

restore parameter.question: The [$t(strength2)] tab looks wrong and I can't get it back to normal.
restore parameter.answer: After making lots of changes to the parameter settings, you may lose track of what you changed. When that happens, press the [$t(initialize all parameters)] button at the bottom of the [$t(parameter)] tab. Your box will not be cleared, so there is nothing to worry about.

tips.question: I want to know about handy features.
tips.answer: There are [i] icons all over the app. Tapping one shows details about the calculations and extra settings. Feel free to explore them.
